description: Curated starting materials. Every entry names where its numbers came from, and a derived entry records how it was derived.
disclaimer: status='tabulated' is a standard's own table. status='measured' is the MEAN of a named test campaign and is NOT a characteristic or design value -- a mean yield exceeds the nominal and is unconservative if used as a design strength. status='indicative' is a typical published figure for the grade. Only 'tabulated' is a design value; check everything else against the governing standard or the mill certificate.

materials.name: AA 6061-T6 wrought (indicative)
materials.standard: ANSI H35 / Aluminum Standards and Data
materials.notes: Typical room-temperature wrought-alloy values. These are widely corroborated typical room-temperature values, not minimums. The authoritative tables are in the Aluminum Association's licensed Aluminum Standards and Data, which this entry does not reproduce; take product-specific minimums from there or from a certificate.

materials.name: AA 7075-T6 wrought (indicative)
materials.standard: ANSI H35 / Aluminum Standards and Data
materials.notes: Typical room-temperature values, not structural design minima. 7xxx alloys require explicit corrosion, fatigue and stress-corrosion checks.

materials.name: EN AW-5083-H116 plate (marine, indicative)
materials.notes: 0.2% proof 215 MPa is the EN 485-2 minimum for H116 plate; tensile 305 MPa sits inside the 290-360 MPa range quoted for the temper. Elastic constants and density are the conventional wrought-aluminium values. Replace with EN 485-2 for the exact thickness or a mill certificate before design. The originally cited hydro.com page is dead and was replaced.

materials.name: EN AW-6082-T6
materials.notes: 0.2% proof 310 MPa and tensile 340 MPa from the supplier datasheet, which does not separate tempers; EN 1999-1-1 characteristic values for design are lower and depend on product form and thickness. Poisson ratio 0.33 is the conventional value for wrought aluminium. No hardening curve: none was available from a citable source.

materials.name: EN-GJS-400-15 ductile iron (indicative)
materials.notes: Representative minimum strength class values with typical elastic constants. Casting section size and heat treatment matter; compression and tension behaviour need not be symmetric.

materials.name: IM7/8552 UD lamina, RTD (measured mean)
materials.standard: NMS 128/2 material spec, NPS 81228 'M' cure; ASTM D3039 / D3518
materials.notes: Room-temperature-dry campaign means from the NCAMP/NIAR Hexcel 8552 IM7 unidirectional qualification programme, generated under FAA oversight. In-plane constants E1, E2, G12 and nu12 are measured; E3, nu13, G13, nu23 and G23 are NOT measured and follow from an assumed transverse isotropy about the fibre axis. Composite failure is not isotropic yielding, so this entry carries no yield stress and defines no failure criterion: take strengths and B-basis allowables from the statistical analysis report NCP-RP-2009-028. A campaign mean is not a design allowable.

measurement.data_report: NCAMP CAM-RP-2009-015 Rev A (22 April 2011), sections 2.3.1, 2.3.2, 2.3.5
measurement.citation: National Center for Advanced Materials Performance (NCAMP), National Institute for Aviation Research, Wichita State University. Hexcel 8552 IM7 Unidirectional Prepreg qualification: data report CAM-RP-2009-015 Rev A and statistical analysis report NCP-RP-2009-028 Rev B. Generated under FAA oversight per NCAMP SOP NSP 100.

calculation.measured: E1, E2, G12, nu12 (RTD means, converted from Msi at 1 Msi = 6.894757 GPa)
calculation.assumption: transverse isotropy about fibre axis 1: E3=E2, nu13=nu12, G13=G12
calculation.nu23: assumed 0.45; not measured by the qualification programme

materials.name: EN 1.4462 (Duplex 2205) nonlinear indicative
materials.standard: EN 10088-4; curve form based on EN 1993-1-4 Annex C
materials.notes: Representative annealed duplex values. n=7 is assumed. Welding condition, product thickness and direction can materially change proof strength and ductility. The cited source supports the curve FORM (Ramberg-Osgood per EN 1993-1-4 Annex C) and the fy/fu inputs; the tabulated points below are computed from those, not taken from the source.

calculation.conversion: engineering to true stress/true plastic strain

materials.name: EN 1.4307 (304L) annealed, nonlinear indicative
materials.standard: EN 10088-4; curve form based on EN 1993-1-4 Annex C
materials.notes: Indicative Ramberg-Osgood engineering curve, converted to true stress versus true plastic strain. n=6 is an explicit modelling assumption; replace fy, fu and n with certificate/test values. The cited source supports the curve FORM (Ramberg-Osgood per EN 1993-1-4 Annex C) and the fy/fu inputs; the tabulated points below are computed from those, not taken from the source.

materials.name: EN 1.4404 (316L)
materials.notes: Modulus 200 GPa and density 8000 kg/m3 from the supplier datasheet. 0.2% proof 220 MPa is the commonly quoted characteristic value for the grade; EN 10088-3 gives 500-700 MPa tensile, and the lower bound is used here. Austenitic stainless has markedly non-linear behaviour well below the proof stress, so a linear-elastic idealisation is conservative in stiffness terms only. No hardening curve: none was available from a citable source.

materials.name: EN 1.4404 (316L) annealed, nonlinear indicative
materials.standard: EN 10088-3; curve form based on EN 1993-1-4 Annex C
materials.notes: Adds a nonlinear counterpart to the existing elastic 316L entry. n=7 is an explicit assumption. Do not treat this as a certified batch curve. The cited source supports the curve FORM (Ramberg-Osgood per EN 1993-1-4 Annex C) and the fy/fu inputs; the tabulated points below are computed from those, not taken from the source.

materials.name: A992 Gr.50 W14X82 flange (measured mean)
materials.notes: W14X82 flange. Campaign MEAN of measured tension coupons, not a characteristic or design value: the mean yield exceeds the grade's nominal yield, so using it as a design strength is unconservative. Intended for validating a nonlinear model against the tests it came from. Elastic modulus is the measured mean and carries real scatter.

measurement.citation: Hartloper, A. R., Ozden, S., de Castro e Sousa, A., & Lignos, D. G. (2022). Database of Uniaxial Cyclic and Tensile Coupon Tests for Structural Metallic Materials (v1.0.0) [Data set]. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.6965147. Licensed CC-BY-4.0.
